lines.text: How many times can the state try you for the same crime? Curtis Flowers was tried six times. By the same prosecutor.

Winona, Mississippi, 1996. Four people are shot inside Tardy Furniture — including a sixteen-year-old new hire. Police fix on Curtis Flowers: a local gospel singer, no criminal record, fired from the store two weeks earlier.

No weapon was ever found. The key witness, a jailhouse informant, later admitted on tape: that was a lie. Doug Evans tried him six times. Four convictions, every one thrown out. Two hung juries. Across those trials the state struck forty-one of forty-two Black jurors.
In 2019, the Supreme Court called it a relentless effort to keep Black citizens off the jury. In 2020 the charges were dropped for good.
Nearly twenty-three years, most of them on death row. The murders are still unsolved. And the prosecutor was never charged, never disciplined. Follow for the cases they don't teach you.
